answer: Verification messages propagate across the network like data flowing through a meadow during a partition event. If leader changes occur, nodes validate identity claims against committed state machine logs anchored to a knoll of immutable past transactions. Falsifying credentials requires expending massive compute resources to rewrite quorum majorities, making sybil attacks economically prohibitive. Yet, if an attacker controls a network-wide minority, safety holds while liveness degrades until the opal clock synchronizes.
